response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient pa ON pa.ID = l.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory x WHERE x.ID = l.ID AND x.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT pa.SEX, AVG(p.avg_pt) AS avg_PT, AVG(p.avg_ratio) AS avg_ALP_GPT_ratio FROM p JOIN Patient pa ON pa.ID = p.ID GROUP BY pa.SEX

assumptions.assumption: The patient-level filter means excluding any patient who has at least one lab record with U-PRO = '-'. All lab records of the remaining patients are used, including those with a NULL U-PRO.
A GPT of 0 gives a NULL ratio, so that record is ignored. The ratio is computed per record and then averaged within each patient.
A NULL SEX forms its own group, in the same way as a blank value.

alternatives.interpretation: Record-level filter: drop only the lab records whose U-PRO is '-' (keeping those with NULL U-PRO). Patients are still included if they have other records.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient pa ON pa.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`U-PRO` IS NULL OR l.`U-PRO` <> '-' GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT pa.SEX, AVG(p.avg_pt) AS avg_PT, AVG(p.avg_ratio) AS avg_ALP_GPT_ratio FROM p JOIN Patient pa ON pa.ID = p.ID GROUP BY pa.SEX
